# Syllabus {.unnumbered}

[What the four weeks look like]{.subtitle .lead}

A four-week, ungraded elective, delivered over Zoom, for fourth-year medical
students, running October 12 to November 6, 2026. Nothing in the course needs
an install, a paid account, or a real patient.

## The one idea

**It is your job to learn where AI helps your work.** Nobody can tell you in
advance, and the tools change every few months. You find out by trying, often,
on things that matter to you, and you learn where AI fails the same way. This
course gives you a framework, a routine, and people to try things with. Most of
your learning will be your own, done with AI.

The safety rules are short. **Use your university ChatGPT Edu or Copilot
account. Never put real patient information into a course activity. Check what
matters before you rely on it. You sign the note.** What counts as patient
information is on [its own page](patient-information.qmd).

## Your week

There are more sessions on the calendar than anyone needs to attend: talks
from the course director on Monday and Wednesday, guest talks, workshops, and
a hands-on "Watch and do" session on Wednesday afternoons.
**Aim for about 3 hours a week of sessions, live or recorded, chosen by your
interest.** Come to more if you like. The talks are recorded. The week's core
chapter goes with Monday's talk: read it after the talk, or instead of it.

Plan on about 8 to 10 hours a week. The table adds up to 7.5 to 9.5 hours:
about 3 hours of sessions you choose, plus the rest of the week.

| When | What | Expected? | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monday, 10 a.m., 60 minutes, live and recorded | **"How I used AI this week"**: the course director's own real tasks, shown on screen. Then **a talk on the week's core topic**, with live demonstrations | Your choice | 1 hour |
| Wednesday, 10 a.m., 60 minutes, live and recorded | **A talk on a second topic**: a menu chapter, or something beyond the book. Some weeks a guest gives it | Your choice | 1 hour |
| After Monday's talk | The week's **core chapter** | Yes | About 1 hour |
| On your own | **[Learn it with AI](learn-with-ai.qmd)**: use AI to teach yourself something you care about. This is the main hands-on work of the course | Yes | 2 to 4 hours |
| Wednesday, 2 to 3:30 p.m., live and recorded | **Watch and do: try it live, together.** Hands-on, content announced in Canvas | Optional | 90 minutes |
| Through the week | Guest talks and workshops from clinicians and researchers using AI in their work | Your choice | 1 to 2 hours |
| Thursday, 11 to 11:45 a.m., live | **Office hours**, drop in: bring what you are stuck on. Not recorded | Optional | 45 minutes |
| Thursday night | [Learning journal](learning-journal.qmd) entry | Yes | 30 minutes |
| Friday, 60 minutes, live | [Small group](friday-groups.qmd), in one of four time slots you choose: open discussion, with topics you bring. Not recorded | Best effort, in your slot | 1 hour |
| Any time | Chapters from the **menu**, and the [open labs](../appendix/open-labs.qmd) | Optional | As you like |

: Your week, weeks 2 to 4. "Your choice" rows together: about 3 hours a week. All times are Mountain time (Denver). The guest schedule is posted in Canvas. {#tbl-week}

## Week 1: live, October 12 to 16

Week 1 is different from the rest. The course director teaches live every
weekday morning, Monday to Thursday, at 10 a.m. Mountain time (Denver). These
sessions are recorded. The small groups meet for the first time on Friday. Canvas has the current
schedule if anything changes.

| Day | Live session |
|---|---|
| Monday, October 12, 10 a.m. | Welcome: how the course works, and how adults learn best |
| Tuesday, October 13, 10 a.m. | A short history of AI |
| Wednesday, October 14, 10 a.m. | What AI is: from AI to machine learning to deep learning to large language models, with time to try it together |
| Thursday, October 15, 10 a.m. | **Hands-on: set up your learning with ChatGPT.** Bring your ChatGPT Edu account. We set it up together, then use it to research what the field expects and build your own plan for the four weeks. Work through [Plan your four weeks with ChatGPT](../chapters/plan-your-learning.qmd). |
| Thursday, October 15, 11 a.m. | Office hours, drop in. Bring what you are stuck on |
| Friday, October 16 | Small groups, in the time slot you signed up for: introductions, then open discussion |

: Week 1. All times are Mountain time (Denver). {#tbl-week1}

## Weeks 2 to 4: the talks

This is a starting plan, and topics may change. Canvas has the current one.

**Week 2, October 19 to 23: getting good at it**

- Monday: **Getting good answers.** How a chatbot reads your prompt, with a
  live demonstration. Goes with the core chapter, the
  [prompting lab](../chapters/enrichment-prompting-lab.qmd).
- Wednesday: **Professional work with AI: writing and beyond**, with
  co-director Christina Olson.

**Week 3, October 26 to 30: AI and your patients**

- Monday: **Talking with patients about AI**, starting from what patients
  already do with it. Goes with the core chapter,
  [Talking to patients about AI](../chapters/core-patient-communication.qmd).
- Wednesday: to be announced, either **bias and equity** (goes with
  [Bias and equity](../chapters/core-bias-equity.qmd)) or **building a small
  tool live** (goes with [Agentic coding](../chapters/enrichment-agentic-coding.qmd)).

**Week 4, November 2 to 6: responsibility**

- Monday: **Who answers for the note.** Goes with the core chapter,
  [Ethics: what you owe when you sign the note](../chapters/core-ethics-regulation.qmd).
- Wednesday: **Where this is going**, for jobs and for the planet,
  and what you will keep from the course. Goes with
  [Will AI take your job?](../chapters/enrichment-workforce-economics.qmd) and
  [What AI costs the planet](../chapters/enrichment-environment.qmd).

| Week | Core | Menu (choose one or more) |

| 2 · October 19 to 23 | [Prompting lab](../chapters/enrichment-prompting-lab.qmd): getting good answers, and knowing their limits | [Critical appraisal](../chapters/core-appraisal.qmd), [Bias and equity](../chapters/core-bias-equity.qmd), [Grounding AI in real sources](../chapters/enrichment-rag-notebooklm.qmd) |

| 4 · November 2 to 6 | [Ethics: what you owe when you sign the note](../chapters/core-ethics-regulation.qmd) | [Will AI take your job?](../chapters/enrichment-workforce-economics.qmd), [What AI costs the planet](../chapters/enrichment-environment.qmd) |

## Attendance

There is more on the calendar than anyone needs. Aim for about 3 hours a week
of sessions, live or recorded, chosen by your interest. Friday small groups
are best effort: sign up for one time in the Canvas Calendar each week, so
your group can change from week to week. If you will miss
a session, follow your school's process for registering absences.

This is a busy time of year, with interviews and travel. You are taking
responsibility for your own learning, so choose what serves it. The
recordings and the chapters let you catch up.

## Grading

The course is ungraded. The learning journal is marked complete or incomplete,
with a one-line reply in weeks 1 and 2. What goes in each entry is on the
[learning journal](learning-journal.qmd) page.
